channel.title: Spring Security Advisories
channel.description: Level up your Java code and explore what Spring can do for you.

item.title: cve-2026-123886 - HIGH - Spring Data Elasticsearch SpEL Expression Injection through String-based Query Method Arguments
item.dc:creator: Spring
item.content:encoded:
Spring Data Elasticsearch replaces positional placeholders in string-based @Query methods with the method arguments before it evaluates SpEL expressions in the resulting query string. As a result, an argument that contains a SpEL expression is evaluated as part of the query, even if the declared query does not use SpEL.

An application is affected if it passes untrusted input as an argument to a repository query method that declares a @Query with positional placeholders. In that case, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary code in the application, and repeated requests can exhaust memory through the unbounded expression cache.

item.title: cve-2026-41698 - LOW - Spring Vault Path Traversal via unsanitized secret path parameter
item.dc:creator: Spring
item.content:encoded:
Spring Vault's Key/Value accessors perform no validation or normalization of the entity identifier argument before incorporating it into a Vault API URL. A caller-supplied value containing path traversal sequences is not rejected or sanitized and can cause Spring Vault to access or overwrite secrets outside the intended keyspace or mount, if those secrets are reachable by the application's Vault token.

Your application may be affected by this if all of the following are true:

  1. The application uses one of the affected repository or KeyValue accessor abstractions.
  2. The id value is derived from user-controlled input.
  3. The application's Vault token holds permissions beyond a single, tightly scoped keyspace path. Applications whose path values are determined entirely at build time are not affected.
  4. The application uses Vault 1.x. Vault 2.0 and later reject non-canonical or relative paths, so deployments using Vault 2.0 or later are not affected.

item.title: cve-2026-59273 - MEDIUM - Spring Security ELRequestMatcher allows Remote Code Execution via unrestricted SpEL evaluation
item.dc:creator: Spring
item.content:encoded:
ELRequestMatcher evaluates a provided SpEL expression against an unrestricted evaluation context that grants full reflection, type references, and arbitrary method invocation, rather than a context limited to its documented request-matching operations.

Because Spring Framework's data binding auto-discovers a property editor for this type by naming convention, an application that binds untrusted input to a bean property of this matcher type can have that input evaluated as a SpEL expression under this permissive context, if invoked by the application.

This can allow an attacker who controls such bound input to achieve remote code execution in the application's process.
